# visio design

One Vite plugin for a visio site. `visio()` returns the plugins of the other packages in the order they need, applies the Vite settings every site copied by hand, gives `solid()` the starter's defaults, and carries the few facts that more than one part reads.

## Goals

1. A site's `vite.config.ts` names what is particular to the site: its name, locale and image, and the optional packages it turns on. What the crawl and the cache need comes from the route table, and the deployment's facts from the env. Nothing about ordering, deduping or bundler targets.
2. Every site gets every part, and no option switches one off. The route table is always `src/routes.ts`, the tokens always `src/styles/tokens.ts`, the icon artwork always `src/icons/`, client env vars always carry `PUBLIC_`, and Solid always gets the defaults below. An agent cannot remove a part or a guard by a change to one line. `visio` exports `visio()` and the option types only, not the individual plugins.
3. Facts flow through options, not through side channels: the site origin reaches the sitemap and the app the same way.

## Shape

```ts
visio({
  site: { name: "visio", locale: "de_DE", image: "/og.jpg" },
  deploy: vercel(),
  extensions: [sanity()],
});
```

| Option | Part | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `site` | head, `import.meta.env` | `name`, `locale` and `image` unset |
| `deploy` | the output after the crawl | required: `vercel()` of `@visio/vercel`, or `cloudflare()` of `@visio/cloudflare` (Deploying) |
| `aeo` | `@visio/aeo`'s robots rules | `{}`: the AI search and training crawlers may crawl an indexable build; `false` on one disallows them; `Content-Signal` names `ai-train` only when `train` is set (`aeo/DESIGN.md`) |
| `extensions` | the build part of an optional package | none; each package's call gives a `VisioExtension` (Extensions): `i18n()` of `@visio/i18n/vite`, `sanity()` of `@visio/sanity/vite` |

Every build crawls the site and writes the output of its `deploy` package (Deploying). What differs between deployments of one site, such as the Worker's name, comes from the env, never an option of the deploy package's call. `cloudflare()` takes only what is the same in every deployment: a hook after each answer, its service bindings, and what Workers Logs keeps (`cloudflare/DESIGN.md`, Observe). There is one build: until 2026-10-08 a `mode` option and `SITE_MODE` in the shell also gave a static build in `dist/client`, and the router removed the `live` routes from it. Until 2026-10-10 a `prerender` option turned the crawl on, with seed `pages` and a `filter`. Without it the build was a server that nothing deployed, so the option only gave a way to leave the crawl and its guards out. The seeds were redundant, because the router names every route nothing links to, and the filter's one use was links to pages not built yet, which are now `pending` in the route table (`packages/router/DESIGN.md`, Prerender). A config that still passes `prerender` stops with that message. Nothing about the crawl is an option: robots.txt is always written (a `robots.txt` in `public/` wins), the sitemap, `llms.txt` and the AI crawler rules follow from the env (below), and the server-function capture keeps its default. `aeo` only says what the AI crawlers may do; no option turns the Markdown copies or `llms.txt` off.

The tests reach the parts no site may leave out, `styling: false`, `images: false`, `svg: false` and `solid: false`, and a build with no `deploy`, through `plugins()` in `src/plugins.ts`, which is not on the package entry.

## Order

`visio:config`, `visio:prerender-env`, `visio:async-render`, `images()`, `svg()`, `visio:icons`, `styling()`, `visio:aeo:dev` (the dev server's `Accept` for the Markdown copies, `aeo/DESIGN.md`), `solid()`, `router()` with the crawl and `llms.txt`, the extensions' plugins (with `sanity()`, the types, the Studio and the overlay's chunk rule), `visio:middleware` (the middleware chain and the router instance as virtual modules), and last the plugins of the `deploy` package. Styling has to see a page file whole before the router splits it into its `?pick=` variants, and both are `pre` plugins, so order alone decides. The image and svg plugins claim their imports before anything else reads the file. The crawl runs last in the build, and the deploy output is written after it.

## Only through `visio`

A config in `site/`, `lab/` or `studio/` may not import a plugin directly: not `@solidjs/vite-plugin`, and no `@visio/*/internal/` entry, which is where every package keeps its Vite plugin (`packages/oxlint-plugin/DESIGN.md`, Internal entries). A zone of `visio/restricted-imports` bans them: the lint preset (`@visio/oxlint-plugin/config`) for the apps, `oxlint.config.ts` for the Studio. A config that wires these plugins by hand skips every guard of `visio()`: the Solid version check, the env facts, and the crawl's guards.

## What `visio:config` sets

Applied unless the site set the same key itself; the list-valued keys merge with the site's own lists. The plugin is `pre`, like `solid()`, so its config hook runs before the Solid plugin crawls the workspace packages and the crawl sees `optimizeDeps.exclude`.

- `resolve.dedupe: ['solid-js', '@solidjs/web', '@solidjs/router', 'vite']`. Linked from another checkout, the packages would resolve Solid from their own `node_modules`: two runtimes, every context read empty.
- `ssr.noExternal: ['@solidjs/prerender']`. In dev an external package imports `solid-js` through Node and gets the production server build while the app runs the dev build.
- `optimizeDeps.include: ['solid-js', '@solidjs/web', '@solidjs/web/server-functions', '@solidjs/prerender']`, the client runtime pre-bundled in one pass on a fresh cache. The dep scanner only sees what `src/` imports; `@solidjs/web/server-functions` is imported by the pre-bundled `@solidjs/prerender`, so without the list the first page load discovers it, re-optimizes, and reloads the browser mid-hydration. An entry the site has not installed is dropped, so Vite does not warn that it cannot resolve it. `@solidjs/router` is left out on purpose: its `solid` condition is JSX source the Solid plugin compiles, so the plugin excludes it from the optimizer and an include entry would undo that. The Solid plugin adds `solid-js/refresh` and, in dev, `@solidjs/diagnostics/browser` and `@solidjs/diagnostics/protocol` itself.
- `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['oxc-parser', '@vercel/functions']`. In dev the Solid plugin inlines the `@visio` packages and lists their dependencies for pre-bundling, server-only ones too. The parser and its wasm chunk would land in `node_modules/.vite/deps` for a browser that never imports them. `@vercel/functions` is worse: the pre-bundle put code it shares with `@sanity/client/stega` in its chunk, so the browser ran its top level, threw `process is not defined`, and the page did not hydrate.
- `server.forwardConsole: { unhandledErrors: true, logLevels: ['error', 'warn'] }`. The dev server prints the browser's uncaught errors, unhandled rejections, `console.error` and `console.warn` in its terminal, with the stack mapped to the source. Vite turns this on only when it detects an agent from the environment. An agent reads the terminal and not the browser console, so visio turns it on for every session. A site that sets `server.forwardConsole` keeps its own levels, but a config that turns it off (`false`, or `{ enabled: false }`) stops with an error.
- `build.target: 'esnext'` and `build.assetsInlineLimit: 0`, so every asset stays a hashed file.
- `envPrefix: 'PUBLIC_'`, always: `src/env.ts` names its client vars with it. A site config that sets another prefix stops with an error.
- `define`: `import.meta.env.SITE_URL` (the origin or `''`), `import.meta.env.SITE_INDEXABLE`, `import.meta.env.SITE_NAME` and `import.meta.env.SITE_LOCALE` (`''` when unset) and `import.meta.env.SITE_IMAGE` (`null` when unset). `visio/client` types them.

## The env read in `@solidjs/prerender`

`posture()` in the client of `@solidjs/prerender` reads `import.meta.env` as one object. Vite then inlines the whole env into that chunk, `MODE: "production"` included. When the chunk also holds app code, the leak scan of the Solid plugin stops the build on each server env value that is equal to an inlined value, for example a `SANITY_DATASET` of `production`. `visio:prerender-env` rewrites that read in the client build to two member reads, `import.meta.env.PRERENDER_MODE` and `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`, so only those two values are inlined. It looks at every JS file of the package, so the read is found when it moves to another file. When a file still reads `import.meta.env` as a whole after the rewrite, in a form the plugin does not know, the build stops: report it to visio and pin `@solidjs/prerender` to the last version that built. A package that reads only by member passes.

## In-order pages

A page written to a file gains nothing from streaming. In Solid's default `stream` render mode, a `<Loading>` boundary still pending when the shell goes out is written as an empty placeholder, and its content comes after `</html>` in a `<template>` that a `$df()` script moves into place. A read that the render starts itself, one that is not in the route's preload, often ends after the shell. A file with that form paints the page without the boundary's content, then shifts everything below it when the script runs, and the browser finds an image in the template late. So every page that becomes a file renders in Solid's `async` mode: the render waits for every boundary and writes one document in order, with no placeholders and no swap scripts. The hydration data is the same.

- **The crawl.** `settleCrawl` from `@visio/router/internal/crawl`, first in the chain, sets `event.renderMode = 'async'` on a request with the crawler's `x-prerender` header. A site's middleware runs after it. Any visitor can send that header too and get the `async` render, on a live route as well: a slower first byte for that request, and nothing more.
- **Vercel's cache.** The function's entry passes `renderMode: 'async'` to `handleRequest` for a cached path, so a page Vercel renders again after it expires or is purged is in order too. The `Render` entrypoint of the Cloudflare Worker does the same for every path it caches. Live routes and draft mode still stream.
- **A fix in `@solidjs/web` 2.0.0-rc.14 to rc.20.** The `async` mode is not safe with two renders in flight, which the crawl (8 pages at a time) and a Vercel instance both have. `renderToStream` keeps its render in a module-scope `sharedConfig.context`, and its thenable resolves the page's holes without making its own render current again, as `pipe()` does in `doShell()`. A page that renders after an await then registers its boundaries with the other render: its placeholder stays, or the other render never settles and fails with "boundary discovery did not converge". `visio:async-render` adds that one assignment to the server builds of `@solidjs/web`. When the code no longer reads as it does in rc.20, the build stops if the installed version is still rc.20. On another version the plugin warns once and leaves the code alone; `test/async-render.test.ts`, which crawls two such pages at once, says whether the fix is still needed.

Until rc.14, cached pages streamed on purpose: in rc.10 the `async` mode left out the query values of a page with no other data, and the browser fetched each again to hydrate. In rc.14 a page in `async` mode hydrates with no extra request.

## The entry script

`@solidjs/vite-plugin` writes the client entry into the head as `<script type="module" async>`, so it can run while the parser is still in the body. Since `@solidjs/web` 2.0.0-rc.15, hydration that starts then waits for a marker that `<HydrationScript />` writes at the end of the shell, so `src/document.tsx` must render `<HydrationScript />`. A streamed page starts to hydrate at the end of its shell, not when its stream ends.

## Solid versions

Once the config is resolved, before any file is compiled, `visio:config` checks that the site runs the Solid visio is built for: the `solid-js`, `@solidjs/web` and `@solidjs/router` the site has installed, against this package's peer ranges, which are the versions the packages are tested with. An older package, or a `@solidjs/web` that is not the `solid-js` release, stops the build with the `bun add` line that fixes it. A newer one is untested and gets a warning. The Solid plugin compiles JSX against the runtime of its own release, and on a mismatch the build fails with dozens of `MISSING_EXPORT` errors that never name a version while the typecheck passes. A Solid bump raises the peer ranges with the pins. A package the site has not installed is left to Vite's own error.

## `solid()` defaults

`ssr: true`, `diagnostics: true`, start mode with `node_modules/visio/src/chain.ts` as the middleware, and server functions with `node_modules/visio/src/server-config.ts` as the configure module. The chain (`virtual:visio/middleware`) runs `settleCrawl` first (In-order pages), then the `deploy` package's middleware when it has one (Deploying): `vercelCache` of `@visio/vercel` puts `@vercel/functions` on the request event as the cache `tagCache()` and `purgeCache()` of `@visio/router` use, and the Worker of `@visio/cloudflare` passes its own, then `liveLists`, which answers the sitemap and `llms.txt` of a deployment with a route that announces (Live lists), then `markdown` from `@visio/aeo`, which answers the Markdown copy of a page (`aeo/DESIGN.md`), then the extensions' middleware (Sanity's routes), then the site's `src/middleware.ts` when it has one, then the `api()` routes of `src/routes.ts`. Every site gets it, so the dev server dispatches API routes and no-JS form posts through the handler like production (a page render still needs a request that accepts HTML, the plugin's own rule). The configure module registers the router that `defineRoutes()` makes in `src/routes.ts` (`virtual:visio/router`) as the single-flight collector, so an action's response carries the refreshed `query()` data. A missing `src/routes.ts` stops the config with the line to write, and a `src/server-config.ts` of the site's own stops it too: until 2026-10-07 every site wrote that file, the same four lines, and so did its `src/middleware.ts` for the API routes. File names are kebab-case, and the Solid plugin looks for `src/Document.tsx` only, so the config passes `src/app.tsx` and `src/document.tsx` to it by name. A `src/App.tsx` or `src/Document.tsx` stops the config with the name to use (`SHELL_NAME_CASE`); the names are read from the folder, because a macOS disk matches either case. The files are looked for under the Vite root, once the config is known, so `vite build site` from another folder finds them. A site cannot change these; the server functions keep Solid's endpoint, `/_server`, which the Vercel output caches reads under.

## Extensions

An optional package turns on with its call in `extensions`, and `visio()` names no package. `visio` has no dependency on any of them, so a site that does not use Sanity does not install it. A `VisioExtension` gives:

- `name`, its npm name, for the messages;
- `routes`, its checks and facts of the route table, and `integrations`, its parts of the crawl (`packages/router/DESIGN.md`, Extensions);
- `plugins`, its Vite plugins, after the router's;
- `served`, paths it serves itself: the router stops on a route of the site's own under one (`ROUTE_RESERVED`, with the extension's name), the crawl skips a link to one, and in dev `.visio/paths.json` lists them for the smoke run;
- `middleware`, a module whose default export goes on the chain after the Markdown copies and before the site's own;
- `app`, a single-page app it serves, which the output answers under its path with its `index.html`, and `open`, paths the password gate lets through. Both reach the `deploy` package as `DeployFacts` (`studioPath`, `open`);
- `languages`, the site's languages, and `connect`, which `visio()` calls once with them before the build starts, so `sanity()` checks the Studio's languages against `i18n()`'s with no import between the two (`sanity/DESIGN.md`, Languages).

Until 2026-10-26 Sanity had an option of its own, `studio`, and `visio` depended on `@visio/sanity`. A config that still passes `studio` stops with `STUDIO_MOVED` and the `sanity()` call to write. `packages/sanity/DESIGN.md` explains what `sanity()` gives.

## Live lists

The crawl writes `sitemap.xml` and `llms.txt` from the pages it rendered, so a document published after the deploy would wait for the next build to be listed (#366). With a route that announces (`router/DESIGN.md`, Prerender), the deployed server answers both paths itself:

- **At build.** `visio:lists` (`lists-build.ts`) is a crawl integration after the extensions' and ahead of the output. In an indexable build with an origin, and only for a list the crawl wrote (a `public/llms.txt` stays the file), it keeps the entries of every page that no announcing route matches. The output gets them as `DeployFacts.lists`, and its entry sets them as the global `Symbol.for("visio.lists")` before the server's first request: the server bundle is built before the crawl, so no import could hold them.
- **At runtime.** `liveLists` (`lists.ts`), on the chain after the deployment's middleware and ahead of the Markdown copies, answers `/sitemap.xml` and `/llms.txt`: the build's entries, plus each page `announce()` gives now with its facts, without a `noindex` one. The formats are the crawl's (`@visio/router/internal/sitemap`, `@visio/aeo/internal/llms`), so with nothing published since the build the answer is the build's file, byte for byte. The reads of `announce()` tag the response as they tag a page, so the publish purge refreshes both lists. Without the global (the dev server, the crawl), the request goes on.
- **Cost.** One `announce()` read per route on a cache miss, never one per page: a head per page would cost a read per page, and the Workers free plan gives a request 10 ms of CPU and 50 subrequests. The facts of `announce()` give the new pages their `lastmod`, title, description and language versions, and the crawl checks them against each page's head (`ANNOUNCE_HEAD_DIFFERS`).
- **Gaps.** A page the build rendered that is not under an announcing route keeps its build entry, so a dynamic route whose pages the crawl found by links alone stays as of the build. No check warns about it: the router cannot tell a route whose pages come from a CMS from one whose pages come from code, which only change with a build. The router skill says to give a CMS route `announce`.

## The site facts

The facts of the deployment are not options. `visio:config` reads them from the env with Vite's `loadEnv` (the `.env` files for the mode, and the shell), once Vite knows the mode: `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` and `PUBLIC_SITE_INDEXABLE`. They differ between a preview and production, so the env is where they are set, and until 2026-10-07 every site's `vite.config.ts` read them with `loadEnv` and passed them on. Now a `site.url` or `site.indexable` in the config stops it with the variable to set. The sitemap and `robots.txt` read the origin when the crawl ends, since the plugins exist before the env is loaded.

- `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` becomes the sitemap's hostname when the deployment is indexable, and the app's `import.meta.env.SITE_URL`: `@visio/router` gives every page a canonical and `og:url` of its own path and makes relative image URLs absolute against it.
- `site.name` and `site.image` are every page's `og:site_name` and social image unless the page sets its own. `image` is an absolute URL or a path under `public/`, resolved against the origin.
- `site.locale` is every page's `og:locale`, and a page cannot set its own. It is `ll_CC`, such as `de_DE`; another form, `de-DE` among them, stops the config with the value to write. The site's and the lab's `src/document.tsx` take `<html lang>` from its language (`de_DE` gives `de`), or `en` without it.
- `PUBLIC_SITE_INDEXABLE=true` lets search engines index the deployment. Unset, or `false`, the deployment is not indexed, so a preview host is never indexed by omission; another value stops the config. On Workers Builds, only a build of the production branch is indexable (`cloudflare/DESIGN.md`, Indexing per branch). A deployment that is not indexable gets no sitemap, no `llms.txt` and no AI crawler rules in `robots.txt`, and `@visio/router` puts `robots: noindex` in every page's head, whatever the page's own meta says. On Vercel, `visio()` does not read `VERCEL_ENV`: Vercel sets the variable per environment, so set it for Production only. The app reads `import.meta.env.SITE_INDEXABLE` for anything else that should differ on a host search engines must not see.

## Icons

A site built on visio shipped the blue placeholder favicon of the visio site for weeks, and nobody saw it. The rule: visio does what is standard and needs no taste, and the site keeps the design decisions. So the site supplies the artwork, and the build writes the files and the links.

- **The artwork** is in `src/icons/`, as the document shell is `src/document.tsx`. `icon.svg` is the tab icon. `icon-dark.svg` is optional: the tab icon on a dark theme. `icon-ico.svg` is optional: the drawing for `favicon.ico`, with any background drawn in. The ICO has no dark variant, so a transparent dark mark disappears on a dark tab in a browser that shows the ICO; this file lets the designer give it a tile. Without it, the ICO comes from `icon.svg`. It does not come from the touch file, whose padding is drawn for the home screen and makes the mark small at 16 px. `icon-touch.svg` or `icon-touch.png` is optional: the touch and app icons, with the background and the padding drawn in. visio decides no padding, no background, no colour, and nothing about how the mark looks at 16 px. Without a touch file, `icon.svg` is used as it is for every size. When it leaves a corner clear, the touch and app icons show that clear corner, so the build prints one `[visio]` line that says so. A drawing opaque at its four corners (a mark on a square drawn to the edge) already has its background, and the line is not printed: `fillsCorners()` in `@visio/image-optimizer` renders it at 64 px and needs each corner pixel fully opaque (alpha 255), so a background at 0.99 opacity or inset by a fraction of a pixel still gets the line. No file name or option says so instead, because the drawing does. Another file name in the folder (`ICON_NAME_UNKNOWN`), a variant without `icon.svg` (`ICON_SVG_MISSING`), or two touch files (`ICON_TOUCH_TWICE`) stops the config. The scratch files of editors (a name that starts with `.` or `#`, or ends in `~`, `.swp` or `.tmp`) are left out, so the dev server does not restart on them. Artwork that is not square, or that has `<text>`, stops the build with the file's name (`ICON_INVALID`). Every SVG in the folder gets the checks, also one that is never drawn as a PNG, such as the dark variant.
- **The files**, at the root of the site: `favicon.ico` (16, 32 and 48 px, from `icon-ico.svg` or else `icon.svg`), `icon.svg` (with the dark variant inside it, behind `prefers-color-scheme`), `apple-touch-icon.png` (180 px), `icon-192.png` and `icon-512.png`, and `manifest.webmanifest`. The fixed names are necessary because browsers ask for `/favicon.ico` and `/apple-touch-icon.png` without a link. `@visio/image-optimizer` converts (`packages/image-optimizer/DESIGN.md`, Icons). The client build emits the files, so the Vercel output (`static/`) and the Cloudflare output (`assets/`) both copy them with the rest of the client build. The dev server makes them on the first request and serves them from memory. An edit to the artwork makes them again. A file added to or removed from `src/icons/` restarts the server, because the links change.
- **The manifest** has `name` from `site.name`, `start_url` from the Vite `base`, and the two icons. It has no `theme_color`, `background_color`, `display` or `short_name`: these are design decisions. A site that needs them has no artwork in `src/icons/` and writes its own manifest.
- **The links** come from the router, as the other site-wide head tags do. `visio:icons` defines `import.meta.env.VISIO_ICONS`, and the `Router` of `src/routes.ts` registers the links in the head of every page (`packages/router/DESIGN.md`, Meta). The site writes no link. The `sizes="32x32"` on the ICO link keeps Chromium from taking the ICO over the SVG.
- **The checks.** A check fires, and a comment in the starter does not. With artwork, a generated file name in `public/` (`ICON_IN_PUBLIC`) or an icon `<link>` in `src/document.tsx` (`ICON_LINK_HANDWRITTEN`) stops the config: the two would fight. Without artwork, a `public/favicon.ico` or `public/apple-touch-icon.png` that is the visio site's old placeholder (compared by sha256, `PLACEHOLDERS` in `src/icons.ts`) stops a build (`FAVICON_PLACEHOLDER`), because otherwise it ships and nobody sees it. In dev it is a warning. A build without artwork also warns when the site has no favicon (`FAVICON_MISSING`), no touch icon (`TOUCH_ICON_MISSING`) or no manifest link (`MANIFEST_MISSING`). The site can still work without them, so these are warnings.

## Deploying

`deploy` is required, and it takes the call of a deploy package: `vercel()` of `@visio/vercel` (`vercel/DESIGN.md`) or `cloudflare()` of `@visio/cloudflare` (`cloudflare/DESIGN.md`). There is no default and no detection from the env: the site names its target, and installs only that target's dependencies. Until 2026-10-13 both outputs were inside `visio`, `deploy` was `'vercel'` (the default) or `'cloudflare'`, and every site installed `@vercel/functions`. A config that still passes the string stops with `DEPLOY_NEEDS_PACKAGE`, and one with no `deploy` with `DEPLOY_MISSING`.

The call returns a `Deployment` (`src/deploy.ts`, the entry `visio/internal/deploy`):

- `output(facts)` gives the crawl integration that records what the output caches, and the plugins that write the output. `visio()` calls it with `DeployFacts`: where the Studio is, the paths the gate lets through, and the route table's `RouteFacts`, which the router fills before the crawl. The integration is the crawl's last, after the extensions' ones, and the plugins are the last of the list, so the output is written after the crawl.
- `middleware`, a module whose default export is a middleware. `virtual:visio/middleware` puts it after the crawl's render mode and ahead of the Markdown copies, so it can put the platform's cache on the request event before anything tags or purges (`router/DESIGN.md`, The cache).

The rest of `visio/internal/deploy` is what both outputs share: the crawl record and `cachedPaths()`, `cacheable()`, `buildPlugins()` (the server bundled with every package and Node's list of built-ins, the client's `prerendered()` reads sent to the server, and the base check), `gated()`, `EXPIRATION`, the security headers, and the version helpers. `@vercel/functions` stays in `optimizeDeps.exclude` as a name, so a Vercel site's dev server does not pre-bundle it, and the name costs nothing where the package is not installed.

The password gate is in the output: `SITE_PASSWORD` set at build time turns it on, on either target, and there is no option in `visio()`. Each package's DESIGN.md says how its output holds the gate.

## Releases

A project gets the packages as files, from a GitHub release of this repo. The repo is private, and the client of a project must not need access to it. So the project commits the packages in `vendor/visio/`, and Vercel, CI and the client need no token. Issue #200 lists the options we rejected: a git dependency (Bun cannot install a subfolder), a registry (tokens, and Node does not strip types under `node_modules`), a link, and a fork.

- **A release** comes from the `release` workflow, started by hand on `main` after CI passed on that commit. The tag is the UTC time, `v2026.10.08-1432`: no semver until visio is stable. `scripts/release.ts` runs `bun pm pack` in each package (the `files` field keeps the tests out, and pack writes real versions in place of `workspace:*` and `catalog:`). It unpacks each package into `vendor/visio/<dir>/` and writes `vendor/visio/manifest.json`: the tag, the commit, the catalog, the Solid versions from `bun.lock`, and the sha256 of each file. The asset is `visio.tar.gz`, and its paths start with `vendor/visio/`. The workflow makes a draft: a draft is not the latest release, so `visio:update` does not install it. Its notes are the squash-merge subjects since the last release, with the `!` subjects (`refactor!:`) under "Breaking". We rewrite them by hand with the rules below, then publish the release. In this repo, `/release` (`.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md`) does all of it.
- **In a project**, the packages are workspaces (`vendor/visio/*`), as in this repo. A folder outside `node_modules` keeps the `.ts` source working: Node strips types there, and oxlint loads `@visio/oxlint-plugin` on Node. The first install is `gh release download -R darkroomengineering/visio -p visio.tar.gz -O - | tar -xz`, then `bun vendor/visio/visio/bin/visio-vendor.ts update`. After that, `bun run visio:update [tag]` installs a release, the latest without a tag. It downloads with the developer's own `gh` login and replaces `vendor/visio/`. Every later step runs in the new release, as `visio-vendor.ts sync` in a child process: the running process has the replaced release loaded, and up to v2026.10.25-0202 that old code wrote the project files, so a new script reached a project one update late (#369). The sync writes into the root `package.json`: the workspace, the `visio:update` and `visio:check` scripts, a `smoke` script for the smoke run (`bin/visio-smoke.ts`) unless the project has a script of that name, the catalog, and the Solid versions as `overrides`. Then it prints the notes of the releases it skipped, and runs `bun install`. The notes come first because a project that depends on a package the release removed gets an install that fails, and the Breaking entry that fixes it must show before that. Before the install, it writes each package's `bin` into its workspace entry in `bun.lock`. Bun does not read a workspace's bin again, not even with `--force`. So `visio-sanity`, which release v2026.10.09-2034 added, was not linked, and that release's notes had a manual step. Deleting the entry instead makes Bun resolve the package's dependencies again, and other versions move.
- **The skills** come with the release. `visio:update` links each `vendor/visio/<dir>/skills/<name>` as `.claude/skills/<name>`, a relative symlink, as in this repo. It links the skills of all packages, not only the packages that the project uses: a skill also tells the agent what not to use (the `animate` skill bans GSAP), and a package that the project adds later has its skill at once. The update replaces a link into `vendor/visio/` and removes one whose target is gone from the release. Two packages with a skill of the same name stop it. It does not touch a directory or a link to a different location: that is the project's own skill, and the update prints a line that it skipped it. It always prints one line with the number of linked skills and the links it added, changed or removed, so the output shows that the step ran. The project commits the links. `visio:check` does not look at them: a link that is missing is not an edit to the release, and the next update makes it again.
- **The notes** are for the agent in a project, and they stack: a project that skips releases reads them all, so each is short and exact.
  - The headings are `## Breaking`, `## Features`, `## Fixes` and `## Optional`, in that order. Leave out a heading with no entry.
  - An entry is one or two lines: what a project sees, with the exact error text or identifier (`optimizeDeps.exclude`, `syncProject()`), and the PR number. The cause stays in the PR (`gh pr view <n>`).
  - Steps go only under Breaking, which a project must do, and Optional. Leave out a change that only affects this repo.
  - `visio:update` prints the notes of each release after the installed one up to the new one, merged by heading, so Breaking comes first.
- **The Solid pins** are necessary because a project has no copy of this repo's `bun.lock`. Without them, a new install took `@solidjs/babel-plugin` rc.14 through the `^` range of `@solidjs/vite-plugin`, next to the rc.13 runtime, and the build stopped on `MISSING_EXPORT ssrStyleProperties`.
- **No edits in `vendor/visio/`.** `bun run visio:check` compares the files with the manifest and fails with `VENDOR_EDITED` on each difference; the project's CI runs it. An update with edits stops, so the edits are not lost. A change goes into this repo, then a release, then an update. So a project cannot drift, and each fix reaches every project.
- **A project extends `visio/tsconfig.base.json`**, and its lint config extends `preset()` from `@visio/oxlint-plugin/config`. The `visio` package depends on `@types/bun`, so a project gets the Node and Bun types that the packages and `vite.config.ts` need without its own `@types/node`.
- **A project's formatter and linter skip `vendor/visio`.** Put it in `ignorePatterns` of `oxfmt.config.ts` and `oxlint.config.ts`. Without it, a project format config that is different from this repo's changes the vendor files, and `visio:check` fails on edits that no one made.

## The smoke run

`bun run smoke` (`src/smoke/`, the `visio-smoke` bin) is the check of what only an open tab shows; `skills/visio/references/smoke.md` is what it reports. The crawl is the build's (prerender-crawler over HTTP), so a page the smoke run reaches is a page the build prerenders. The dev server it starts runs as indexable, so only a page's own `noindex` skips the SEO description check. A page that answers an error, or a link to a path that does not exist, is a finding on the page that links to it, because that is the file to fix. With `site`, a word in the loaded page that the server HTML lacks is a finding: no AI crawler but Google's and Apple's runs scripts. Chrome is driven over the DevTools protocol with Bun's `WebSocket`, so the package has no browser dependency, only a Chrome binary (`CHROME_PATH`). A project's `smoke` script wins over visio's, and a `smoke` script that starts with `bun vendor/visio/` is visio's own from an earlier release, so an update rewrites it.

## Not yet built

- Image widths from the styling screens. The default list covers phone, tablet, laptop and their 2x up to 4K, and `sizes()` already narrows what each image gets from the tokens; deriving the list from the breakpoints would need a rule for full-bleed images, which render wider than any breakpoint. Left on the defaults until a site shows the need.
- A `fonts` option. Fonts are declared in the tokens and subsetted by the styling plugin; there is nothing to configure at this level today.
